one_liner: MongoDB's C library for building and iterating BSON; in one third-party C shootout it round-trips faster than cJSON on 4 of 5 payloads.
what_it_does: libbson builds, parses, validates and iterates BSON, MongoDB's length-prefixed binary document format, and converts BSON to and from (Extended) JSON. Documents are written with bson_append_* calls (or BSON_APPEND_* macros, plus bson_array_builder_t for arrays) and read with a bson_iter_t cursor; there is no DOM and no schema. It is not a drop-in for a JSON library: the wire format, API and data model (typed int32/int64/double/decimal128/ObjectId/date fields) are all different.
how_it_is_fast: A bson_t carries a 120-byte inline buffer, so small documents are built without any heap allocation; appends memcpy little-endian scalars into one contiguous buffer and back-patch the length prefix. Reading is zero-copy: bson_init_static wraps an existing buffer and bson_iter_t walks it in place with no allocation, returning pointers into the buffer for strings and sub-documents. Against text JSON the gain comes from skipping number formatting/parsing and string escaping, not from any clever search; key lookup (bson_iter_find) is a linear scan.
when_to_use: You already talk to MongoDB or store BSON and need a C serializer that matches the server's format byte for byte.
You want a self-describing binary document format with typed fields (int64, decimal128, dates, binary) instead of JSON text, and can afford larger output.

Write-heavy C code that today formats JSON with cJSON, json-c, jansson or parson: in the GLD shootout libbson serializes 1.5x to 10x faster than cJSON on message, document, telemetry and event (derived from page data).
You need in-place, allocation-free iteration of received documents (bson_init_static + bson_iter_t) rather than building a tree.
when_not_to_use: You want the fastest C serializer of any format: in the same run mpack, msgpack-c, flatcc, the protobuf rows and libcbor's streaming encoder all beat libbson on every payload.
You need the fastest JSON: yyjson round-trips faster than libbson on document, telemetry, strings and event (for example telemetry 357,412 ns vs 962,634 ns at 100 instances).
Payloads dominated by strings or by arrays read element-by-element: libbson lost to cJSON, json-c and parson on the strings payload (1,168,630 ns vs cJSON 669,472 ns).
Compactness matters: BSON stores array indexes as decimal key strings and fixed-width integers, so output was 1.2x to 1.7x larger than CBOR or MessagePack and larger than JSON text on three payloads.
Out-of-memory handling matters: libbson's own docs say it calls abort() on OOM rather than returning an error.

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (built from mongo-c-driver with CMake; libbson can be built alone, target bson_static / bson::static in 2.x)
integration.dependencies: none beyond libc (part of the mongo-c-driver source tree; libmongoc is optional)
integration.platforms: cross-platform C: Linux, macOS, Windows (MSVC) and other POSIX systems; little- and big-endian handled in the byte-order layer
integration.thread_safety: not documented as a guarantee for shared objects; bson_t and bson_iter_t are plain caller-owned structs with no internal locking, so share them across threads only with external synchronization; the global allocator vtable (bson_mem_set_vtable) is process-wide

gotchas: Harness flaws behind the numbers: the GLD wrapper (c/src/serializers/ser_libbson.c) reads array element i with bson_iter_init_find on the key "i", a linear scan from the array start, and copies every scalar element into a freshly bson_init'ed wrapper document that is then destroyed; the writer formats every array key with snprintf instead of libbson's bson_uint32_to_string table or bson_array_builder_t, and writes every integer as INT64. cJSON's reader also walks its linked list per index (cJSON_GetArrayItem), so the index pattern is shared, but the wrapper documents and key parsing are libbson-only costs that probably explain the strings loss.
BSON arrays are documents keyed "0", "1", ...; there is no O(1) indexing, so iterate once with bson_iter_next instead of looking up indexes.

Small documents live in the bson_t's inline buffer and spill to the heap when they grow, so bson_destroy() is required even for stack-declared documents; bson_init_static wrappers must not outlive the buffer they point into.

Security fixes keep landing: CVE-2025-0755 (bson_append_* could write past the buffer near the INT32_MAX size limit) was fixed in 1.27.5, the version benchmarked; CVE-2024-6381 and CVE-2024-6383 hit bson_strfreev and bson_string_append (per secondary CVE aggregators, not NVD). The 2.x line removed bson_as_json and renamed the CMake package and targets.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick libbson over libcbor or flatcc only when the consumer is MongoDB or another BSON reader; on raw speed and size libcbor's streaming encoder (1.4x to 5.5x faster round trip in the same run) and flatcc (document 75,146 ns vs 546,018 ns) both win.
verified_claims_summary: GLD.SerializerBenchmark's C suite (run 2026-09-29-182101, gcc 11.4.0, i7-12800H on the powersave governor, IQR-filtered means) timed libbson 1.27.5 from mongo-c-driver against C JSON libraries on five fixed payloads: at 100 instances libbson's serialize plus deserialize was 1.55x to 3.2x faster than cJSON 1.7.19 on message, document, telemetry and event but 1.75x slower on strings; all rows passed the suite's fidelity check (1.0). The project makes no speed claim, the comparison is cross-format (BSON vs JSON text), and libbson is slower than every MessagePack, protobuf and FlatBuffers row in the same run.
status_note: The listed mongodb/libbson repository has been archived since 2020-10-13 (last code 1.9.0, 2017); the maintained libbson lives in mongodb/mongo-c-driver under src/libbson (Apache-2.0, 883 stars, commits as recent as 2026-10-09, releases 2.5.6 and 1.30.13), with bugs tracked in MongoDB's CDRIVER JIRA rather than GitHub issues.
